topic: Shared-assay sharp probability-of-benefit envelope. In a blinded binary-outcome RCT, let one nondifferential assay channel with sensitivity s and specificity c be shared across arms, with (s,c) in a fixed rectangle and s+c-1>=kappa>0. Let the closed four-type potential-outcome law satisfy finite cross-product odds-band inequalities. Derive the unique compatible quadratic root and prove every sharp endpoint of P(Y(0)=0,Y(1)=1) is computed from at most ten explicit channel candidates (hence at most fourteen): feasible polygon vertices, stationary-line/edge contacts, and one possible kappa-edge point. Construct attaining laws; for the strictly positive finite-log-odds model prove equality of infimum/supremum and an exact endpoint-attainment criterion. With independent trial arm binomials and a blinded gold-standard assay-validation sample, invert exact primitive confidence sets and project the finite candidate map to cover the full sharp interval uniformly through contacts and tied optimizers, with excess width O(1/(kappa sqrt(Nmin))). Consumer: a prospective validation-enabled replication or reanalysis of the Polack et al. BNT162b2 endpoint workflow. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Independent algebra derived the compatible p11 root, marginal derivative bounds, factored stationary resultants, a conservative ten-candidate endpoint classification, strict-attainment criterion, explicit witness endpoints (sqrt(193)-5)/48 and 4/15, four-piece exact confidence projection, and uniform Clopper-Pearson/Hoeffding excess-width control. Two hundred twenty population optimizations agreed within 4.435e-11; one generic optimizer missed a legal boundary minimum that the explicit enumeration recovered, reinforcing the need for certified edge handling. No exact primary-source collision was found; assay transport remains an explicit prospective assumption. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Mechanize the finite-candidate completeness lemma across theta=1, marginal contacts, and strict-compatible representatives, then implement outward-rounded certified feasibility and projection arithmetic. EARLY KILL TEST: Reproduce the recorded kappa-edge confidence-projection instance whose legal vertex gives benefit about 0.1320580555; any implementation returning the failed generic optimizer's 0.1443566356 must stop and repair its edge enumeration. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/pid_sharedassay_benefit_envelope.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the sharp probability-of-benefit interval when both randomized-trial arm outcomes are observed through one shared nondifferential binary assay whose sensitivity and specificity lie in a rectangle with a positive Youden-index lower bound, while the latent four-type potential-outcome table obeys a finite cross-product-odds band.

source_refs.claim: Probability of benefit is not identified in a binary-outcome RCT, and candidate dependence parameters can be incompatible with the full observed-data law.
source_refs.author: Iuliana Ciocănea-Teodorescu, Erin E. Gabriel, and Arvid Sjölander

source_refs.claim: Models dependence between binary potential outcomes through an odds ratio but assumes the endpoint itself is observed rather than assay-misclassified.
source_refs.author: Zhiwei Zhang, Lei Nie, Guoxing Soon, and Aiyi Liu
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series C

source_refs.claim: Represents discrete misclassification as a linear system and derives identification regions for functionals under restrictions on the misclassification matrix.
source_refs.author: Francesca Molinari

open_problems.why_unsolved: The literature treats dependence-sensitive probability of benefit and discrete misclassification separately, but the scan found no result joining them under a common uncertain assay channel. The usual fixed-marginal reconstruction must be replaced by a joint affine inversion through the same sensitivity and specificity, so separate armwise extrema are not sharp. The cross-product band then introduces a probability-compatible latent-cell root and nonlinear semialgebraic optimization whose boundary contacts and stationary points require a completeness argument.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp lower-and-upper endpoint characterization by an explicit finite candidate map, with constructive attaining four-type laws and an exact criterion distinguishing attained extrema from strict-model infima or suprema.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing moves directly from cancellation of benefit and harm to the missing cross-world dependence information.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: An average effect can conceal simultaneous benefit and harm -> probability of benefit depends on the unobserved joint potential-outcome law -> an odds-ratio restriction supplies dependence information -> assay-misclassified arm marginals make compatibility and sharpness the unresolved destination

method_exemplars.technique: Solve the binary 2-by-2 potential-outcome table from its marginals and a specified odds ratio, including selection of the probability-compatible algebraic root.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination has the same latent-cell equation, but its two marginals vary jointly with a shared assay channel.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode misclassification through a channel matrix and establish sharpness by exhausting latent distributions satisfying the induced restrictions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This supplies the assay-inversion and constructive-sharpness machinery absent from probability-of-benefit sensitivity analyses.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate sharp treatment-effect-distribution bounds and analyze nonsmooth endpoint inference using fewer-than-n bootstrap arguments when the standard bootstrap fails.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The shared-assay endpoint is likewise a switching extremum over multiple candidate branches.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop finite-sample exact or uniformly honest confidence projection for the full shared-assay sharp probability-of-benefit interval that remains valid when endpoint candidates tie, contact a feasibility edge, or collapse at a boundary.

source_refs.claim: Probability-of-benefit bound estimators can exhibit ordinary-bootstrap undercoverage at or near parameter-space boundaries.
source_refs.author: Erin E. Gabriel, Michael C. Sachs, and Andreas Kryger Jensen

source_refs.claim: Establishes asymptotic laws for sharp treatment-effect-distribution bounds and notes possible failure of the standard bootstrap.
source_refs.author: Yanqin Fan and Sang Soo Park

source_refs.claim: Provides uniformly asymptotically valid calibrated projection for smooth functions of parameters constrained by finite moment equalities and inequalities.
source_refs.author: Hiroaki Kaido, Francesca Molinari, and Jörg Stoye

open_problems.why_unsolved: The endpoint is a minimum or maximum over channel-boundary, vertex, and stationary candidates, so its active branch changes at ties and tangencies. Existing benefit-bound work documents bootstrap nonregularity, while calibrated projection is generic and asymptotic. Neither line supplies finite-sample coverage that exploits independent trial-arm and gold-standard validation binomials, nor a uniform excess-width guarantee as assay informativeness approaches its allowed lower bound.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A confidence procedure covering the entire sharp interval through all optimizer ties and boundary contacts, with finite-sample or uniform asymptotic validity and an explicit excess-width bound in the trial size, validation size, and Youden-index lower bound.

writing_exemplar.why: It connects sharp probability-of-benefit bounds to practical interval estimation and foregrounds boundary-driven bootstrap failure.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Sharp bounds are the scientifically relevant estimand -> plug-in endpoints inherit max-min nonsmoothness -> ordinary bootstrap coverage can fail near boundaries -> assay-validation uncertainty requires contact-robust projection

method_exemplars.technique: Derive directional endpoint limit laws and use fewer-than-n resampling to accommodate nondifferentiable extrema.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems estimate treatment-effect-distribution endpoints formed by switching minima and maxima.

method_exemplars.technique: Calibrate a target-specific projection by checking feasibility of relaxed moment restrictions and prove uniform coverage over a class of data-generating processes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The assay rectangle, validation constraints, odds band, and latent-law restrictions form a finite-dimensional projection problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct confidence intervals for interval-identified scalar parameters whose coverage remains appropriate as identification-region width changes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The shared-assay interval can shrink, widen, or collapse at candidate contacts.

open_problems.open_problem: Partially identify probability of benefit when assay sensitivity and specificity are learned from an external gold-standard validation sample but may differ in the trial population within a bounded transportability model.

source_refs.claim: External-validation sensitivity and specificity require transport assumptions when error-related covariate distributions differ between validation and study populations.
source_refs.author: Rachael K. Ross, Stephen R. Cole, Jessie K. Edwards, Paul N. Zivich, Daniel Westreich, Julie L. Daniels, Joan T. Price, and Jeffrey S. A. Stringer

source_refs.claim: Validation must estimate the false-positive and false-negative parameters needed for quantitative correction; one predictive value is inadequate.
source_refs.author: Stephan Lanes and Daniel C. Beachler

open_problems.why_unsolved: Ross et al. identify risks and risk differences under point transport conditions and standardization, but probability of benefit additionally depends on cross-world association. Under bounded rather than exact assay transport, the trial channel becomes set identified and must be optimized jointly with the odds-restricted four-type law. The first proof step that changes is substitution of transported sensitivity and specificity: it becomes a feasible transport set whose projection through the benefit functional is nonlinear.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp identified interval for probability of benefit over trial-specific assay channels satisfying an explicit bounded transport model, together with a confidence projection accounting jointly for trial, validation, and transport uncertainty.

writing_exemplar.why: It explains both the attraction of inexpensive external validation and the additional assumptions needed to transport measurement-error parameters.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Outcome error threatens causal analyses -> external validation can learn assay parameters at lower cost -> population differences invalidate direct transport -> bounded transport uncertainty must enter the probability-of-benefit region

method_exemplars.technique: Transport measurement-error parameters through covariate standardization or iterated outcome modeling under explicit exchangeability and positivity conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These transport maps supply the center and limiting conditions for a partially transported assay set.

method_exemplars.technique: Treat validation information as restrictions on a misclassification matrix and optimize functionals over compatible latent distributions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Bounded transport converts validation estimates into restrictions rather than point-known channel entries.

method_exemplars.technique: Calibrate projection critical values for a scalar functional instead of projecting an unnecessarily large joint confidence region.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target endpoint projects trial, validation, and transport nuisance restrictions into one scalar.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the sharp probability-of-benefit envelope when outcome misclassification may be treatment-arm-specific, with separate sensitivity-specificity rectangles linked by a prespecified nondifferentiality-departure constraint and a finite odds band on the latent potential outcomes.

source_refs.claim: Outcome-misclassification correction generally requires false-positive and false-negative parameters for each comparison group.
source_refs.author: Stephan Lanes and Daniel C. Beachler

source_refs.claim: Develops finite-population sensitivity analysis for binary outcome misclassification in randomized experiments through adaptive integer programming.
source_refs.author: Siyu Heng and Pamela A. Shaw
source_refs.venue: Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics

open_problems.why_unsolved: A shared blinded channel yields two nuisance coordinates, whereas controlled arm departures introduce four accuracy coordinates and destroy the common affine inversion behind a low-complexity polygon. Heng and Shaw optimize misclassification patterns for randomization tests rather than a superpopulation joint-potential-outcome estimand, while Lanes and Beachler motivate group-specific error parameters without deriving sharp benefit-type bounds. The scan found no treatment of their interaction with an odds band on the latent four-type law.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp semialgebraic characterization of the probability-of-benefit endpoints, with attaining laws and either a finite endpoint-enumeration theorem or a counterexample proving that constant-size enumeration fails beyond a shared channel.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames endpoint misclassification as a threat to causal conclusions despite random assignment and distinguishes arm-specific error mechanisms.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Randomization prevents confounding but not endpoint error -> arm-specific false positives and negatives can alter conclusions differently -> validation should target consequential error mechanisms -> sharp benefit bounds under controlled differential channels are missing

method_exemplars.technique: Represent arm-specific classification matrices as simultaneous linear restrictions on latent probabilities and prove sharpness through feasible latent distributions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The direct-misclassification representation accommodates distinct channel matrices before the nonlinear association restriction is imposed.

method_exemplars.technique: Adaptively reformulate a large integer program to locate worst-case arm-by-error-direction configurations under randomized assignment.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its computational reduction is structurally analogous to searching the expanded differential-channel boundary for extremizing latent laws.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct uniformly valid calibrated-projection intervals by extremizing a target over relaxed sample moment constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The differential-channel model is a finite-dimensional projection problem with changing active restrictions.

open_problems.open_problem: Extend shared-assay probability-of-benefit bounds to an ordinal endpoint observed through a common uncertain multicategory confusion matrix, while imposing explicit total-positivity or local cross-product-ratio bands on the joint ordinal potential-outcome table.

source_refs.claim: Derives sharp symbolic benefit bounds for ordinal outcomes in observational and imperfect-randomization settings, but not under an uncertain outcome-misclassification channel.
source_refs.author: Erin E. Gabriel, Michael C. Sachs, and Andreas Kryger Jensen

source_refs.claim: Derives sharp benefit and no-harm bounds for ordinal potential outcomes from fixed marginals and additional joint-distribution restrictions.
source_refs.author: Jiannan Lu, Peng Ding, and Tirthankar Dasgupta
source_refs.venue: Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics

source_refs.claim: The direct-misclassification framework covers finite-support variables but does not specialize to ordinal cross-world benefit bounds.
source_refs.author: Francesca Molinari

open_problems.why_unsolved: For binary outcomes the joint table has one association coordinate and the odds restriction reduces to a quadratic cell equation. With K ordinal levels there are multiple association coordinates, the shared confusion matrix is a constrained stochastic matrix, and total-positivity or local-odds restrictions interact with transportation-polytope constraints. Existing ordinal-benefit results expose growing symbolic complexity without misclassification, while multicategory channel methods do not address the cross-world target.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp linear or polynomial-program characterization of the ordinal probability-of-benefit region, with constructive attaining couplings and symbolic endpoint formulas or certified finite candidate sets for fixed small K.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the closest motivation and notation for ordinal benefit, no-harm, and relative-treatment-effect bounds.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Ordinal outcomes make mean effects hard to interpret -> benefit probabilities retain patient-level meaning -> cross-world dependence prevents identification -> an uncertain shared multicategory assay adds a coupled identification layer

method_exemplars.technique: Express ordinal benefit as mass above the diagonal of a coupling table and derive sharp extrema over a transportation polytope.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination has the same ordinal coupling target after its marginals are constrained through a shared confusion matrix.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent multicategory classification by a stochastic matrix and combine channel restrictions with latent-distribution feasibility.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the natural assay layer to compose with the ordinal transportation problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive limit laws for estimated sharp treatment-effect-distribution bounds and handle ordinary-bootstrap failure with fewer-than-n resampling.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Ordinal endpoint formulas are maxima and minima of many pieces, producing analogous boundary and tie nonregularity.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize covariate-adjusted sharp probability-of-benefit bounds when one assay channel is shared across covariate strata but latent potential-outcome dependence is restricted by a single marginal odds-ratio band rather than separately chosen stratum-specific odds ratios.

source_refs.claim: Covariate-dependent odds-ratio sensitivity analysis becomes high dimensional, motivating simpler fixed-parameter implementations.
source_refs.author: Zhiwei Zhang, Lei Nie, Guoxing Soon, and Aiyi Liu
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series C

source_refs.claim: Uses one marginal sensitivity parameter independent of covariate dimension but identifies compatibility with the observed law as a substantive restriction.
source_refs.author: Iuliana Ciocănea-Teodorescu, Erin E. Gabriel, and Arvid Sjölander

source_refs.claim: Develops consistent linear-program estimation of fraction-who-benefit bounds with baseline covariates and support restrictions on the joint potential-outcome law.
source_refs.author: Emily J. Huang, Ethan X. Fang, Daniel F. Hanley, and Michael Rosenblum

open_problems.why_unsolved: Conditional benefit bounds can be computed stratumwise when each stratum receives its own fixed association parameter. A single marginal dependence restriction instead couples the strata, and the common assay channel adds another global coupling because every observed conditional risk is inverted with the same sensitivity and specificity. Consequently, neither stratumwise linear programming nor fixed-odds reconstruction separates; compatible conditional laws must jointly satisfy a global marginal association constraint.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp functional characterization of the covariate-adjusted probability-of-benefit interval under global dependence and shared-assay constraints, with compatible attaining conditional laws and an estimator with a valid limit or confidence result.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the tradeoff between high-dimensional conditional association parameters and one interpretable marginal sensitivity parameter.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Baseline covariates can explain effect heterogeneity -> stratum-specific association models become unwieldy -> one marginal sensitivity parameter avoids dimensional explosion -> a shared imperfect assay creates a global compatibility problem

method_exemplars.technique: Recover stratum-level joint binary potential-outcome probabilities from conditional marginal risks and an odds-ratio specification.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These conditional reconstructions are the local building blocks to be coupled by the marginal band and shared channel.

method_exemplars.technique: Use covariate-indexed linear programs and prove consistency under restrictions on the joint potential-outcome support.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination retains the covariate-adjusted benefit target but replaces separable fixed marginals with globally coupled assay-corrected marginals.

method_exemplars.technique: Establish asymptotic distributions and resampling inference for covariate-adjusted sharp treatment-effect-distribution bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a limit-theory template once the globally constrained endpoint functional is characterized.

literature_map:
Tian and Pearl (2000, UAI; arXiv:1301.3898) and Gadbury, Iyer, and Albert (2004, JSPI, DOI 10.1016/S0378-3758(03)00115-0) established the foundational nonidentification and sharp-bound problem for binary benefit types.
Molinari (2008, Journal of Econometrics, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2007.12.003) supplied a general direct-misclassification framework based on restrictions on a channel matrix.
Fan and Park (2010, Econometric Theory, DOI 10.1017/S0266466609990168) derived sharp treatment-effect-distribution bounds and documented possible standard-bootstrap failure.
Zhang, Nie, Soon, and Liu (2013, JRSS C, DOI 10.1111/rssc.12012) used an odds ratio to model cross-world dependence and noted the dimensional burden of covariate-dependent specifications.
Huang, Fang, Hanley, and Rosenblum (2017, Biostatistics, DOI 10.1093/biostatistics/kxw049) developed consistent LP estimation for fraction-who-benefit bounds with covariates and joint-law restrictions.
Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta (2018, JEBS; arXiv:1507.01542) derived sharp ordinal benefit and no-harm bounds from fixed potential-outcome marginals.
Fay et al. (2018, Statistics in Medicine, DOI 10.1002/sim.7799) distinguished causal probability-of-benefit estimands from independent-draw Mann–Whitney estimands and supplied interval procedures.
Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019, Econometrica; arXiv:1601.00934) provided uniformly valid calibrated projection for finite moment-(in)equality models.
Polack et al. (2020, NEJM, DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2034577) is the motivating observer-blinded BNT162b2 trial with laboratory-confirmed binary Covid-19 endpoints but no probability-of-benefit analysis.
Lanes and Beachler (2023, Pharmacoepidemiology and Drug Safety, DOI 10.1002/pds.5601) argue that validation must learn the relevant false-positive and false-negative parameters in each comparison group.
Ross et al. (2024, Epidemiology, DOI 10.1097/EDE.0000000000001701) show that external-validation sensitivity and specificity require transport assumptions when error-related covariates shift.
Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen (2024, Biometrika; arXiv:2305.10555) extend sharp symbolic benefit bounds to ordinal and imperfect-randomization settings and discuss boundary-sensitive inference.
Ciocănea-Teodorescu, Gabriel, and Sjölander (2025, Biostatistics, DOI 10.1093/biostatistics/kxaf011) develop marginal dependence sensitivity analysis and identify compatibility with the full observed law as a key issue.
Heng and Shaw (2025, JCGS; arXiv:2201.03111) analyze randomized-experiment outcome misclassification by adaptive integer programming under finite-population randomization inference.
Across these papers, benefit-type dependence, assay misclassification, validation transport, and robust inference are mature separately; the scan found no primary-source result combining a shared uncertain assay, finite latent odds band, constructive sharpness, finite candidate completeness, and contact-robust exact projection.
